B4: Abstract Data Types

HL Only | 23 hours

Unit Overview

In this HL-only unit, you learn how more advanced abstract data types are used to organise and access data efficiently. You study linked lists, binary search trees, sets and hashing.

Unit Objectives

What students are expected to know:

  • what an abstract data type is and why ADTs matter
  • how linked lists are structured and manipulated
  • how binary search trees support efficient searching
  • how sets and hash-based structures work
  • how these structures compare in terms of use, performance and implementation

Unit Outcomes

What students are expected to be able to do:

  • explain the properties and purpose of ADTs
  • evaluate and apply linked lists
  • explain binary search trees
  • construct and apply sets
  • explain core hashing ideas and the principles behind ADT implementation

Subtopics

B4.1

Fundamentals of ADTs — ADT principles, linked lists, binary search trees, sets and hashing
